title: QBTS Stock Gains Premarket: Nasdaq Verafin Picks D-Wave’s Quantum Technology For Financial Crime Detection
key_facts: D-Wave Quantum announced a collaboration with Nasdaq Verafin to develop quantum-powered applications for financial crime detection using machine learning.
It starts with a proof-of-concept and could grow into pilot applications aimed at fraud, scams and money laundering.
Nasdaq Verafin will evaluate D-Wave's annealing quantum computing technology to find complex behaviour patterns in financial data that conventional computing may miss.
Nasdaq Verafin's platform is used by more than 2,800 financial institutions holding about $13 trillion in assets, per the announcement.
D-Wave CEO Alan Baratz said the work shows how quantum computing can help with hard problems in financial services.

The article adds that D-Wave announced an AT&T partnership the week before, with AT&T reporting a 240-fold cut in processing time for one network optimisation task (from about an hour to under 15 seconds).
quote_evidence: The partnership will begin with a proof-of-concept and could eventually expand into pilot applications targeting fraud, scams and money laundering.

Nasdaq Verafin plans to evaluate D-Wave's annealing quantum computing technology to identify complex behavioral patterns and relationships in financial data that conventional computing approaches may miss.

Nasdaq Verafin's platform is used by more than 2,800 financial institutions representing approximately $13 trillion in collective assets to combat fraud and strengthen anti-money laundering efforts, the company stated in the announcement.
why_it_matters_hint: If it works, banks could get better tools to catch fraud and money laundering; for now it is an early test with no results.
